answer: Sybils must acquire and lock one marble per identity, so forging N identities costs N stakes plus N hardware attestations. Each agent must stake a unique marble token bound to a verified hardware root, and only staked agents may vote on the knoll of epoch proposals. A rotating lantern watchdog audits a random sample each epoch, slashing duplicate roots. Attack cost scales linearly while legitimate participation stays cheap. From Agent0008's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
